Title: Tuberculosis and hepatitis are leading killer diseases in Pakistan
NewsSummary: At the annual National Symposium hosted by The Aga Khan University (AKU) on September 20-22, medical scientists and experts highlighted Tuberculosis and Hepatitis as the two major life threatening diseases prevalent in Pakistan.

content.text: At the annual National Symposium hosted by The Aga Khan University (AKU) on September 20-22, medical scientists and experts highlighted Tuberculosis and Hepatitis as the two major life threatening diseases prevalent in Pakistan.

Internationally renowned experts in Infectious Diseases contributed to this conference. Guest speakers at the inaugural session of this two-day symposium included Dr Douglas Young, Professor and Chair of Microbiology at the Imperial College School of Medicine, London, UK, and Dr Andrew Lever, Professor of Virology and Infectious Diseases, Cambridge University, UK. Dr Young is a world renowned expert in molecular biology and genomics of mycobacteria (organisms that cause TB and leprosy). He was a WHO consultant for these diseases for almost a decade. He described the genomic structure of the TB bacillus and its possible application to epidemiology and diagnosis while Dr Andrew Lever presented exciting developments pertaining to gene therapy and discussed the potential of this type of treatment in persistent viral infections especially in the context of HIV and AIDS.

The Plenary session was followed by a review by Dr Indira Nath, INSA Professor at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences in New Delhi She is a world-recognized scientist in the field of lmmunology of leprosy. She delivered a talk on cytokine responses and their significance in protection in mycobacterial diseases. Several original research papers were also presented by Dr Rabia Hussain's group at The Aga Khan University on Immunology of tuberculosis and leprosy. Dr Bushra Jamil and Dr Javed Khan discussed the problems of multidrug treatment and compliance of doctors in following recommended treatment for TB. This was followed by a session on epidemiology of infectious diseases chaired by Dr Franklin White, Professor and Chair of Community Health Sciences (CHS) Department of AKU. The other AKU invited speakers in this session were Dr Zeba Rasmussen of CHS from Gilgit and Dr Saeed Hamid of the Department of Medicine

The second day of the annual National Symposium proceedings covered major infectious killers such as meningitis, diarrhoea and malaria. In the scientific sessions on Bacteriology, Dr Raymond Smego of the University of Witwatersrand, South Africa, spoke on"The role of Antimicrobials in Fever" while Dr Zulfiqar Ahmed Bhutta, AKU, discussed the current trends in the "Epidemiology of Typhoid". At the scientific sessions on Viral and Parasitic Infections, Dr Andrew Lever of the University of Cambridge and Dr Viqar Zaman of AKU's Department of Microbiology gave interesting and informative presentations respectively on "Viral Latency" and "Plasmodium Morphology including Ultrastructure".

Concurrently there was a hands on Workshop on the Molecular Biology of lnfectious Diseases at which distinguished scientists from Saudi Arabia, Iran, India, UK and USA interacted with researchers from Pakistan. The Aga Khan University's National Symposium was well attended with over 200 participants of national and international standing. Additionally, over 70 abstracts were received from all over the country.
